content:
Democrats enter the final weekend before Tuesday's midterm elections with a lead in national polling — but the voters who have not yet cast ballots look far more evenly divided, and they are the ones who will decide control of Congress.

Emerson College Polling's final national survey, conducted October 24–26 among 1,000 likely voters with a credibility interval of plus or minus 3 points, puts the generic Democratic candidate ahead of the Republican, 52 percent to 42 percent, with President Donald Trump's approval at 37 percent and disapproval at 57 percent.

Cygnal's final National Voter Trends poll, conducted October 23–24 among 1,500 likely voters, also puts Democrats ahead on the generic ballot, 52 percent to 43 percent — but with a sharp split beneath it. Voters who have already cast ballots back Democrats 63 percent to 35 percent. Voters still to vote split 47 percent for Democrats and 46 percent for Republicans, and late deciders lean Republican. Nearly half of Republicans (48 percent) plan to vote on Election Day, compared with 29 percent of Democrats.

Polling averages tell a similar story. The RealClearPolling average puts Democrats at 51.4 percent and Republicans at 43.2 percent, an 8.2-point lead. An NBC News polling average recently had 52 percent of likely voters preferring Democratic control of the House compared with 43 percent preferring Republican control, and POLLSMAX had Democrats at 50.9 percent and Republicans at 42.8 percent.

The stakes on Tuesday, November 3: all 435 House seats are on the ballot. Republicans now hold 219 seats and Democrats 214, with two vacancies, so Democrats need a net gain of just three seats to take the majority. In the Senate, 35 seats are up; Republicans hold a 53–47 majority, and Democrats need a net gain of four seats to reach 51.

Midterm advertising spending has reached $11.2 billion, the highest ever for a midterm cycle. The cost of living is the top issue for voters — named by 34 percent in the Emerson poll and 36 percent in a Harris poll — followed by fighting corruption in government at 28 percent in the Emerson survey.

Polls are snapshots of voter preferences, not predictions: control of Congress is decided race by race. The Cook Political Report says the likeliest House outcome is Democrats winning between 227 and 240 seats.

What it means for readers here

Webb County voters are part of the same Tuesday electorate: the local ballot carries the mayor's race, city council seats, the TX-28 House race and a U.S. Senate seat, and early voting here already closed with 46,332 ballots cast. The national picture says the House leans Democratic; the Cygnal numbers say Election Day itself is still up for grabs.

Sources:

  • QNC News, "Emerson Final Poll Puts Democrats 10 Points Ahead Before Midterms," October 31, 2026
  • Cygnal, "Final Midterm Poll: Dems Bank on Early Lead, Yet-to-Vote Voters Are Tied, Late Deciders Break Republican," October 27, 2026
  • North Jersey, "Are Democrats winning the midterms? Current polls, predictions and odds," October 28, 2026
  • Zark News, "Democrats Lead Final Midterm Polls as Both Parties Make Last Push Before Tuesday's Vote," October 31, 2026

title: Final midterm polls show Democrats ahead nationally — but yet-to-vote voters are tied
